sections.h2: Where Henry County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Henry County deeds are filed in Napoleon, in Suite 202 up the stairs in the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street. The Recorder's number is 419-592-1766, and the counter shuts at 4:30 on weekdays. Nobody is there on weekends or holidays.

One recorder covers all of Henry County, roughly 416 square miles. A farm along the Putnam County line and a house inside Napoleon are handled at the same window. The county's recorder page calls the office custodian of land records. It accepts deeds, mortgages, mechanic's liens, powers of attorney, IRS liens, subdivision plats, military discharges, partnership papers, and the zoning resolutions of the county and its townships.

sections.h2: Why old chains of title matter here
sections.html: Henry County was organized in 1834, so its recorded deeds reach back about two hundred years of farm and town sales. Inherited houses and family farms can carry decades of easements, mortgages and affidavits. A title company digs those out of the recorder's index, so a seller should expect them to come up. Napoleon is the county seat and its biggest city.

The Henry County Auditor works in the same courthouse and can be reached at 419-592-1956. These Ohio sale forms are posted on the auditor's site:

  • DTE 100, the value statement and receipt that goes with a conveyance.
  • DTE 100EX, where you write down why a transfer owes no such fee.
  • DTE 101 for a homestead parcel, DTE 102 for a parcel in the farm valuation program.
  • The Henry County Land Transfer Policy. Ask the auditor's staff for a copy early.

Before the Recorder, the deed goes to the auditor. Under section 319.202 the buyer files a value statement, the auditor endorses the deed, and a rental house triggers an extra landlord filing under Chapter 5323. After that it moves on to the Recorder.

sections.h2: What the Auditor charges on a sale
sections.html:
The auditor's charge comes from section 319.54(G)(3): $1 at minimum, or a dime for each hundred dollars of value if that is more, with part of a hundred counted whole. The seller pays. Get the dollar figure for your price from the counter before closing day.

Any Ohio county may add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. The grantor pays it before the Recorder sees the deed. Ask the auditor whether Henry County levies it, and check that your settlement sheet reflects the answer.

Some transfers owe no statement fee. Examples are a gift deed, a conveyance worth $100 or less, a deed that only pledges the land as security, and a split among one estate's heirs. The reason is written on DTE 100EX.

Fees follow section 317.32. Every charge has a base fee and a matching housing trust fund fee. For the first two pages that is $17 plus $17, and for each later page $4 plus $4. Counties can also add a preservation surcharge, up to $5. The office can quote the total for your deed.

Pages are counted at 8.5 by 14 inches, and the caption page is page one. If a deed runs a few lines onto a third sheet, the cost rises, so keep the format tight.

The state's layout rule in section 317.114 applies too, and some Ohio counties charge $20 for a deed that breaks it. Ask what Henry County adds before you sign one with odd margins or tiny type.

Owners live in about 82.5% of the occupied homes here, and a typical owner-occupied house is valued at $168,600. Just 19 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale seldom competes with new construction, and a nearby farm sale can set the tone for pricing.

About a third of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census and two thirds in rural ones, which is why farm parcels and big lots show up in the recorder's queue as often as town lots.

Online sheriff sales through RealAuction cover orders received after August 1, 2022. Tax sales take place downstairs in the courthouse. Bidders must wire or ACH a deposit, never cash. The deposit depends on the appraised value:

  • $2,000 for an appraisal up to $10,000.
  • $5,000 for an appraisal from $10,000 to $200,000.
  • $10,000 for an appraisal above $200,000.

Following the auction, the buyer waits 30 to 45 days for the court to confirm the sale and for the sheriff's deed. The former owner keeps title until the judge signs, and the new owner gets title only when the sheriff's deed lands in the Henry County Recorder's index. Within 14 days, the judgment creditor and the first lienholder may redeem by paying the clerk of courts the full price.

sections.h2: Property tax help in Henry County
sections.html:
The Treasurer's mailing address is P.O. Box 546, Napoleon, and the phone is 419-592-1851. Monthly payment plans for unpaid back taxes and current taxes halt added interest and penalties. A Tax Installment Prepay plan breaks the annual bill into coupons, and a late coupon draws no penalty as long as each half is paid in full by its closing date.

Henry County has 40 taxing districts, each with its own rate, and taxable value is 35% of market. Reappraisal comes every six years, with an update in the third year. An owner who disagrees with a valuation can file with the Board of Revision between January 1 and March 31. The 2 1/2% owner-occupancy rollback needs one application, due before the first Monday in June.

On the homestead page, the TY2025 figures are a $40,000 income limit and a $28,000 exemption, with more for disabled military service members. Owners who are struggling can contact NOCAC, the Northwestern Ohio Community Action Commission, or Maumee Valley Planning's housing program.

sections.h2: If you owe on the house at closing
sections.html:
Any mortgage balance and unpaid tax are normally paid from your proceeds by the title company, and the lender then records a release. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer ahead of closing. Also ask the auditor if the parcel has a homestead reduction, because DTE 101 then travels with the deed. Carry the parcel number and the legal description from your own deed so staff can match the new deed to the tax record without a callback.

Allow time for each stop. The deed goes to the auditor first, then to the Recorder in Suite 202, and mailing it adds days. A seller who is out of town can ask the closing agent to carry the paperwork across the courthouse.

faqs.q: Who records Henry County deeds, and where?
faqs.a: The Henry County Recorder, in Suite 202 on the second floor of the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street in Napoleon. The phone is 419-592-1766.

faqs.q: Do I visit the auditor before the recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The auditor receives the buyer's statement of value and endorses the deed, then the recorder files it. Both offices sit in the Napoleon courthouse.

faqs.q: How is the Ohio conveyance fee figured?
faqs.a: Whichever is larger: $1, or ten cents for each $100 of value, rounding any part of $100 up. The seller pays it unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: Is there a county transfer tax in Henry County?
faqs.a: Ask the auditor. Ohio allows a county to levy up to thirty cents per $100 after two hearings.

faqs.q: Can a sheriff-sale buyer record immediately?
faqs.a: No. The judge must confirm the sale and the sheriff must receive the deed, which takes 30 to 45 days after the auction. Title passes when the sheriff's deed is recorded.
